text:
maria: FYI seeing a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel routing bump this morning. heatmap + flamegraph attached in the CI logs.

aj: noted. which kernel change specifically? the batch selector or the microkernel rewrite?

maria: batch selector + smaller kernel reordering. perf bot shows more short-lived KV misses. root cause unclear yet.

devon: can you paste the profiler lines? esp the KV lookup times and any Tokenizer ops spikes.

maria: here are the hotspots from the flamegraph snippet:
```
KVCache.lookup  32ms
KernelSelect.choose  6ms
Tokenizer.normalize  18ms
PrefixLookup.canonicalize  41ms
```

katie: PrefixLookup.canonicalize at 41ms is worrying. that step should be cheap (string trim + stable field ordering). did the canonicalizer regressed?

maria: i ran a quick diff against yesterday's canonicalizer; new routing includes additional metadata in the key (route_id, kernel_variant). suspect the ordering changed and tool fields sometimes serialized in different order.

az: @aj any recent changes to tool/function call serialization?

aj: pushed a change to allow unordered tool args (to reduce noise), might be the cause. I thought we canonicalized on the client but maybe not for prefix-cache keys.

zach: if tool args are unordered, the canonicalization needs to sort keys for the cache key. otherwise identical prompts can miss. we should prefer deterministic ordering at the cache key layer.

devon: also saw tokenizer version mismatches in the sample traces: some requests were tokenized with v2.3 and others v2.2 after the canary. token hashes changed.

maria: yup, sample payload shows header `X-Tokenizer-Version: v2.3` dropped sometimes for background jobs. that will flip KV keys.

katie: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pin tokenizer version in warmup/backfill requests, 2) canonicalize tool fields + system prompt block before hashing, 3) roll back the batch-selector tweak for canary nodes.

aj: quick patch to canonicalizer: always stringify `tools` as sorted JSON keys, and include a normalized `sys_prompt_hash`. small snippet:
```
function canonicalKey(req) {
  const tools = JSON.stringify(sortKeys(req.tools || {}));
  const sys = normalizeSys(req.system_prompt || '');
  return hash([req.prompt, tools, req.tokenizer_version || 'v2.3', sys]);
}
```

maria: looks good. but we need to be careful: adding more fields into the key increases cardinality for cold caches. maybe we should keep keys compact: use `sys_prompt_hash` instead of full text and only include `tools` when present.

devon: agree. Also we should avoid relying on client headers for tokenizer_version. runtime should set an explicit token_version field before keying. that's atomic and easy.

zach: ops-bot: can you run a quick synthetic to compare hit-rate delta if we sort tool keys vs leave unordered? small A/B for 10k requests.

ops-bot: scheduled job `cache-key-abtest-5755` enqueued, will run 10k samples across canary and baseline pools and post summary in 15m. :gear:

maria: i started a backfill warmup on the affected nodes with pinned tokenizer v2.2 to see if hit-rate recovers. initial 1k requests show +4% hit-rate but still below baseline.

ak: (typo) meant @aj

aj: thanks. If the abtest shows deterministic ordering wins, i'll cut the canonicalizer patch as a hotfix and push to canary. w/ metrics gating.

katie: longer term: add a `cache_key_version` header we can bump when we change keying rules. makes rollbacks explicit.

maria: agreed. file a short RFC? 1-pager, include migration plan for existing keys (we may need TTL backfill).

devon: also add observability: per-key-component entropy metric (how many unique sys_prompt_hash per prompt) — helps spot runaway cardinality.

zach: if we go ahead with the hotfix, schedule a kernel-revert window as fallback. we should not ship both kernel routing + keying change at once.

maria: plan for today: 1) wait for ops-bot abtest results, 2) if sorting helps, hotfix canonicalizer to sort tool keys + include sys_prompt_hash, 3) pin token_version at runtime, 4) cut canary, monitor hit-rate and latency for 30m, 5) if green, deploy wider.

aj: i'll prep the patch and PR with perf numbers.

ops-bot: abtest finished: sorted-tool-keys -> 9.8% increase in hit-rate over baseline (p<0.01). full summary posted: /ci/cache-abtest/5755/report.html

maria: wow that's convincing. moving forward with hotfix + token_version pin.

katie: i'll start the RFC and add the entropy dashboard.

devon: one more note: let's add a small TTL bump for prefill warmups (2x for 24h) to accelerate hit curve recovery after key changes.

maria: agreed. thanks all. I'll open the follow-ups and tag folks. :thumbsup:
